clue.text: Seafood proving a hit within island quietly wiped out

indicators.note: within says the a-plus-hit pair sits inside what remains of the island
something wiped out is removed entirely, so the letter for quietly is taken away from the island

parts.note: Capri is an Italian island in the Bay of Naples
p (piano) is the musical marking for quietly
to lam is to hit or thrash

explanation.surface: Seafood that proved a smash on a Mediterranean island has all been quietly eaten up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'proving a hit' reads as success, but 'a hit' is A plus the old verb lam; 'wiped out' strips the P, 'within' places the pair.
explanation.definitionFit: Calamari is squid served as food, a familiar kind of seafood.

clue.text: What may be running discomfort?

parts.note: read as a riddle: a sharp pain in the side that a jogger gets, also something done by needle and thread

explanation.surface: A question about the discomfort that comes with going for a run.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden sharp pain in the side, typical of running, has this name.

clue.text: Change of mind in passing document which grinds

indicators.note: in places the rearranged letters inside the document

parts.note: a will is the document that takes effect on someone's passing

indicators.note: a change of the word mind means its letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A change of heart while reading through a paper that grinds someone down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'passing document' is one idea: the paper that acts on a death. 'Change of' scrambles the mind, 'in' houses it.
explanation.definitionFit: A windmill is a machine whose sails drive millstones that grind grain.

clue.text: Warming drink may go cold when lifted

indicators.note: in a down clue, lifted means the words are read from bottom to top

parts.note: can and may both express permission
taken as written
C is the abbreviation for cold, as on taps

explanation.surface: A warming drink might lose its heat once raised from the table.
explanation.walkthrough: 'when lifted' turns the whole run CAN GO C upside down in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Cognac is a French brandy, a spirit drunk to warm oneself.

clue.text: Want to get right, in conclusion

indicators.note: in places the right letter inside the conclusion

parts.note: death is the conclusion of life

explanation.surface: A wish to get things right before the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Want in the sense of lack or scarcity is a synonym of shortage.

clue.text: 1950s' music club set up work

indicators.note: in a down clue, set up means the word is raised, read bottom to top

parts.note: a wood is a type of golf club
op (opus) is a musical work

explanation.surface: A nightclub put together a piece of music in fifties style.
explanation.walkthrough: 'set up' turns WOOD into DOOW in this down clue.
explanation.definitionFit: Doo-wop is the vocal harmony style of rhythm and blues popular in the 1950s.

clue.text: Greeting rogue trader, threw a punch

parts.note: hi is a greeting
a tout sells tickets illicitly at inflated prices

explanation.surface: On meeting a crooked dealer, someone lashed out with a fist.
explanation.definitionFit: To lash out with a fist at someone is the phrasal verb used here, matching the past tense.

clue.text: The relative doctrine

parts.note: taken as written
sis, short for sister, is a relative

explanation.surface: A family member's guiding belief.
explanation.definitionFit: A thesis is a proposition or tenet maintained by argument, much like a doctrine.

clue.text: Eastern chief punches minor, producing shiner

indicators.note: punches means goes into, so the pieces are placed inside the word for minor

parts.note: slight means minor or small
arch as an adjective means chief, as in arch-enemy

explanation.surface: An Eastern boss thumps a child and leaves him with a black eye.
explanation.walkthrough: 'shiner' suggests a black eye from the punch, but here it is anything that shines.
explanation.definitionFit: A searchlight is a powerful lamp, so it shines, making it a shiner in the literal sense.

clue.text: Steamy round watering hole in Australian port

indicators.note: round says the word for steamy is wrapped around the watering hole

parts.note: steamy means hot
a bar is a watering hole, a place to drink

explanation.surface: A sultry bar in an Australian harbour town.
explanation.definitionFit: Hobart is the capital of Tasmania and a harbour city in Australia.

clue.text: Move towards war, or make peace?

definitions.meaning: to put at risk, a step that may bring conflict nearer
split into two words, it means to put a stop to fury

explanation.definitionFit: To put something in danger is the plain sense; split into two words it means stopping rage.

clue.text: Noted conclusion, backing a medic

indicators.note: backing means the words a and medic are read backwards

parts.note: doc is short for doctor, a medic

explanation.surface: A final remark that supports a doctor.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Noted' means in musical notes, not remarked.
explanation.definitionFit: A coda is the concluding passage of a piece of music, a conclusion in notes.

clue.text: Is such fashion, daring to fit in smallest of measurements?

indicators.note: to fit in means the measurement is placed inside the word for daring

parts.note: heroic means daring or bold
the inch is the smallest of the everyday imperial measurements

explanation.surface: A bold fashion that demands squeezing into the tiniest sizes.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Is such' just points to the definition. The surface's tiny clothing sizes are apt, since the look prized extreme thinness.
explanation.definitionFit: Heroin chic was a 1990s fashion look of pale, gaunt models.

clue.text: After shuffling, had led with nifty trick at cards

indicators.note: shuffling, as with a pack of cards, signals the letters are mixed

explanation.surface: Someone shuffled, led a card, and pulled off a slick card trick.
explanation.definitionFit: Find the lady is the three-card trick, also called three-card monte.

clue.text: Source of colouring agent certainly heading for trouble in useless pudding?

indicators.note: in places these letters inside the word for useless

parts.note: duff means useless, and is also a steamed pudding as in plum duff
yes means certainly

indicators.note: heading for means the first letter of the following word, trouble

explanation.surface: A colouring agent apparently brings trouble to a failed dessert.
explanation.walkthrough: 'heading for' takes only the T of trouble; 'pudding' supports the duff, a British steamed suet pudding.
explanation.definitionFit: A dyestuff is a substance from which a dye or colouring is obtained.

clue.text: In which seven bells knocked out of one another?

definitions.text: In which seven bells knocked out of one another?

parts.words: In which seven bells knocked out of one another?
parts.note: seven bells knocked out of someone is a heavy beating, and the name also echoes the sound of bells

explanation.surface: A question about a brawl in which both sides beat each other senseless.
explanation.definitionFit: A noisy fierce fight is called by the imitative name of a chiming bell.

clue.text: Maltose broken down — not quite thus?

definitions.text: Maltose broken down — not quite thus?

indicators.note: a sugar broken down has its letters split and rearranged
not quite means the last letter is missing

explanation.surface: A sugar is digested, though not fully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'not quite' drops the final E of MALTOSE, and 'broken down' rearranges the rest; the whole clue also describes the result.
explanation.definitionFit: Something not quite done is nearly done, so the clue as a whole defines the word.

clue.text: Might this puncture a hole in the sack?

definitions.meaning: a projectile fired from a gun that makes holes
dismissal from a job, as in getting the boot

explanation.definitionFit: A gun's projectile pierces; and being given it means being fired from work.

clue.text: Escort keeps supple, though stupid

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the escort word contains the supple word

parts.note: to bring someone is to escort them along
lithe means supple

explanation.surface: A companion stays flexible despite being dim.
explanation.definitionFit: Blithering is an intensifier meaning utterly foolish, as in a blithering idiot.

clue.text: 'ooligan upset? It's plain to see

indicators.note: in a down clue, upset means the word is turned upside down

parts.note: a hooligan is a hard nut, and the apostrophe shows the H dropped, so ard nut

explanation.surface: A thug, dropping his aitches, gets upset that it's obvious.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' turns ARDNUT upside down in this down clue; the dropped H is a Cockney accent.
explanation.definitionFit: Tundra is a vast treeless Arctic plain.

clue.text: Supporter of an order

parts.note: a band holding up a stocking, also the emblem of England's highest order of chivalry

explanation.surface: Someone who backs a religious or knightly order.
explanation.definitionFit: A band holding up a stocking gives its name to the highest English order of knighthood.

clue.text: The Guardian abroad brings wisdom

definitions.meaning: a newspaper speaks of itself as we, and the French for we is used here

explanation.definitionFit: In British slang the Greek word for mind means common sense; in French it is the pronoun we.

clue.text: Nick put on jumper of the highest quality

indicators.note: put on means placed after, in this across clue to the right of

parts.note: a top is a garment such as a jumper
a notch is a nick or small cut

explanation.surface: Nick pulls on a sweater, which is first-rate.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' looks like a name or a theft; it is a small cut. A jumper is a British sweater.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-notch is an informal adjective for excellent or first-class.

clue.text: Shoot through puzzle

definitions.meaning: to pepper with holes, as with bullets

explanation.definitionFit: To pepper with bullet holes is one sense; an enigma posed as a question is the other.

clue.text: River needs one to cut river tax

indicators.note: to cut means the pieces go into the second river

parts.note: the Taff is a river in south Wales, flowing through Cardiff
the Taff is a river in south Wales, flowing through Cardiff
I is the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A river must pay a levy for crossing another river.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to cut' puts R and I inside TAFF.
explanation.definitionFit: A tariff is a duty or tax charged on imports.

clue.text: Cheese maker asking for money back

indicators.note: back means the word is read backwards

parts.note: a tenner is a ten-pound note, a sum of money

explanation.surface: A cheesemonger wants a refund.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cheese maker' sounds like a person; it is the substance that curdles milk.
explanation.definitionFit: Rennet is the enzyme used to curdle milk in making cheese.
